incidents.title: Checkout timeouts spiking to 30% of requests
incidents.symptoms: p99 latency on /charge jumped from 400ms to 12s. Timeout errors on 30% of checkout attempts. Downstream card processor reporting normal. Started 10 minutes after the 14:00 deploy.
incidents.root_cause: Deploy 2417 introduced an N+1 query in fraud-check that exhausted the connection pool under load.
incidents.resolution: Rolled back deploy 2417; connection pool recovered within 2 minutes. Fix shipped next day with the query batched.

incidents.title: TLS handshake failures from EU merchants
incidents.symptoms: EU merchants receiving SSL_ERROR_HANDSHAKE. US traffic unaffected. Certificate transparency logs show the EU edge cert expired at midnight UTC.
incidents.root_cause: Edge certificate for eu.pay.acme.com expired; auto-renewal job had been silently failing for 3 weeks due to a revoked DNS API token.
incidents.resolution: Rotated the certificate manually, restored the DNS API token, and added alerting on renewal-job failures.

incidents.title: Login failures: token validation rejecting valid sessions
incidents.symptoms: All logins failing with 401 invalid_token. Sessions created before 09:00 validate fine. JWT signature verification failing for new tokens only.
incidents.root_cause: Clock skew: one of three auth pods drifted 4 minutes after NTP was blocked by a new egress firewall rule, so tokens it issued appeared to be from the future.
incidents.resolution: Restarted the drifted pod, fixed the egress rule to allow NTP, added clock-skew alerting.

incidents.title: Order writes failing: disk pressure on primary DB node
incidents.symptoms: INSERT latency climbing, then write failures. DB node disk at 97%. WAL segments accumulating faster than checkpointing could recycle them.
incidents.root_cause: A debug log table added for a one-off investigation was never dropped and grew to 400GB.
incidents.resolution: Dropped the debug table, ran cleanup, added disk-usage alerts at 80% with table-size breakdown.

incidents.title: Search results empty for ~15% of queries
incidents.symptoms: Users intermittently seeing zero results for queries that normally return many. One of six index shards returning empty responses with HTTP 200.
incidents.root_cause: Shard 4 replica desynced after an OOM kill and rejoined serving an empty index while reporting healthy.
incidents.resolution: Forced re-sync of shard 4 from the primary; changed readiness probe to verify document count, not just process liveness.

incidents.title: Email queue backlog: 2M messages and growing
incidents.symptoms: Email delivery latency hours behind. Queue depth growing 500/s. Workers alive but each send taking 30s. SMTP provider dashboard shows our IPs rate-limited.
incidents.root_cause: A marketing batch job triggered provider rate limiting; workers retried with no backoff, keeping us pinned at the limit.
incidents.resolution: Paused the batch job, added exponential backoff with jitter to workers, drained the queue over 4 hours, sharded future batch sends.

incidents.title: Duplicate charges reported by customers
incidents.symptoms: Support tickets reporting double charges. Payment processor shows two identical captures 30s apart for affected orders. Correlated with a network blip causing client retries.
incidents.root_cause: Charge endpoint was not idempotent: client retries after gateway timeouts re-executed the capture instead of returning the original result.
incidents.resolution: Added idempotency keys to the charge flow with unique-constraint dedupe in the transaction; refunded affected customers.

incidents.title: Stock levels drifting negative for hot SKUs
incidents.symptoms: Flash-sale SKUs showing negative stock. Oversold by ~3% on top items. Reads served from a cache updated by two writers racing.
incidents.root_cause: Read-modify-write on stock counts without transactional isolation; concurrent decrements lost updates under contention.
incidents.resolution: Moved decrements into a single serializable transaction with retry-on-conflict; backfilled correct counts from the order ledger.

incidents.title: API 5xx spike after dependency upgrade
incidents.symptoms: 500s at 8% immediately after the morning deploy. Stack traces show serialization errors on the orders response model. No infra changes.
incidents.root_cause: Minor-version bump of the JSON serialization library changed default datetime handling, breaking responses for orders with null shipped_at.
incidents.resolution: Rolled back the deploy, pinned the dependency, added a contract test for the response schema.

incidents.title: Rate-limit storm from misbehaving mobile client
incidents.symptoms: Auth endpoint QPS 20x normal. A specific mobile app version retrying token refresh in a tight loop on every 401. Legitimate users seeing elevated latency.
incidents.root_cause: Mobile release 5.2.1 shipped a retry loop without backoff on token refresh failure; a cohort with revoked tokens created a storm.
incidents.resolution: Rate-limited by client version at the edge, forced upgrade for 5.2.1, added server-side Retry-After headers the client honors.

incidents.title: Search latency degraded after index grew past memory
incidents.symptoms: p95 search latency doubled over two weeks. No deploys correlated. Index size crossed available page-cache memory; disk reads per query climbing steadily.
incidents.root_cause: Organic index growth exceeded node memory; queries went from page-cache-hot to disk-bound.
incidents.resolution: Scaled index nodes up a memory tier and added index-size-to-memory ratio monitoring with a 75% alert.

incidents.title: Push notifications failing for iOS users
incidents.symptoms: iOS push delivery at 0% since 03:00. Android normal. APNs returning 403 InvalidProviderToken.
incidents.root_cause: APNs auth key was revoked when a departing employee's Apple Developer account was deactivated; the key had been created under their personal account.
incidents.resolution: Generated a new APNs key under the org account, rotated it into the service, audited other credentials for personal-account ownership.

runbooks.title: Runbook: Checkout latency / timeout spikes
runbooks.body:
1. Check deploy timeline — was there a deploy in the last 30 min? If yes, compare p99 before/after.
2. Check connection pool saturation (active vs max connections) on the gateway and fraud-check.
3. Check downstream processor status page.
4. If deploy-correlated: rollback_deploy first, investigate later.
5. If pool-saturated without a deploy: flush_connection_pool, then find the slow query.
6. Verify recovery: p99 under 800ms for 5 consecutive minutes.

runbooks.title: Runbook: Duplicate charge reports
runbooks.body:
1. Pull processor capture records for affected orders; confirm duplicate captures and their spacing.
2. Correlate with gateway timeout/retry logs — duplicates usually follow client retries after timeouts.
3. Verify idempotency keys are being generated AND enforced (unique constraint, same transaction as the capture record).
4. Refund duplicates via the bulk refund tool; notify support with the affected-order list.
5. Never disable retries as a fix — fix idempotency instead.

runbooks.title: Runbook: Sudden widespread 401s / token validation failures
runbooks.body:
1. Determine scope: all tokens or only recently issued ones? Only-new points at issuance; all points at validation config.
2. Check clock skew across auth pods (compare NTP offsets) — skew breaks iat/exp validation.
3. Check for recent key rotation; verify JWKS endpoint serves the current key set.
4. Drifted clock: restart_service on the affected pod and confirm NTP reachability (egress rules).
5. Add skew alerting if not present.

runbooks.title: Runbook: Database disk pressure
runbooks.body:
1. Identify biggest tables and recent growth (table-size breakdown, not just total disk).
2. Look for debug/temp/log tables that should not exist in prod.
3. Check WAL accumulation vs checkpoint rate.
4. Free space fastest-first: drop known-junk tables, then archive cold data.
5. Do NOT expand disk as the first move if growth is anomalous — find the source.
6. Alert at 80% with per-table attribution.

runbooks.title: Runbook: Delivery queue backlog
runbooks.body:
1. Measure inflow vs drain rate — backlog math tells you if you must act or can wait.
2. Check provider rate-limit status before scaling workers: more workers against a rate limit makes it worse.
3. Identify the inflow source (batch job? incident-driven spike?) and pause it if batch.
4. Ensure workers back off exponentially with jitter on provider 429s.
5. scale_up only after the rate limit is cleared.
6. Post drain-ETA to the incident channel hourly.
